ops_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the initial workspace setup for {{vendor}}, our chosen project-management tracker, so a human teammate can quickly sign up and approve it. Please do NOT attempt to sign up, authenticate, accept terms of service, or create the workspace yourself — account creation and approval remains a human step.

First, ask me for any missing inputs: our company/workspace name, the initial team name(s) we want (e.g. Engineering, Product), the labels we typically use (bug, feature, chore, etc.), the workflow statuses we want (e.g. Backlog, Todo, In Progress, In Review, Done), and whether we're importing data from another tool (and if so, which one and where the export file lives).

Using those inputs, prepare a complete setup packet: a proposed workspace name, team structure with owners, a label list, a workflow status list mapped to our process, 2-3 relevant project templates to jumpstart initial projects, and a short guided-walkthrough checklist an engineer could follow during first-time setup (steps like: create workspace, add team, configure labels, set workflow statuses, create first project from template, import legacy data if applicable). If we mentioned migrating from another tool, also draft a brief import plan noting what data types (issues, statuses, labels, projects) need mapping.

Organize all of this into a single clear document or checklist I can hand to the approving teammate, with every field pre-filled where possible so they only need to review, sign up, authenticate, and click through the actual workspace creation and approval.

When finished, report back with: the full prepared packet (workspace name, teams, labels, workflows, templates, import plan if relevant), and then explicitly stop for human sign-off — do not proceed further or attempt any part of the actual account creation.

ops_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure custom workflow states in {{vendor}}, our project tracker, as part of setting up projects/teams/labels/workflows. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/team name(s) or URL, and (2) the workflow states I want per team (e.g., Backlog, Triage, Todo, In Progress, In Review, Done, Canceled, or any custom names/order/categories reflecting our actual process). If I haven't given you a specific workflow yet, propose a sensible default set of states (with categories: backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled) for a typical software team and ask me to confirm or edit it before proceeding.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s API and, for each team/project I specify, prepare the exact set of workflow state changes needed: which states to add, rename, reorder, or mark as default/completed states, matching the confirmed list. Do NOT apply any changes yet. Instead, produce a clear preview/checklist showing, per team: current states vs. proposed states, with additions, renames, and ordering changes clearly marked.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, present this checklist to me and then stop for human sign-off — do not create, update, or delete any workflow states until I explicitly approve the plan. Once I confirm, wait for my explicit go-ahead before executing the changes via the workflow-state creation/update operations in {{vendor}}.

Report back with: the full proposed workflow-state plan per team, any ambiguities or missing info you need me to resolve, and a note confirming you are paused awaiting my approval.

ops_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up our project tracker in {{vendor}}. Approval is required before any changes go live, so your job is to PREPARE a full plan for teams and projects, then stop for human sign-off — do not create anything until I explicitly approve.

First, ask me for any of the following if you don't already have them: our {{vendor}} workspace/organization name, the list of teams we want (e.g. Engineering, Product, Design), the list of projects under each team, and any known priorities, owners, or target dates for those projects.

Then produce a draft configuration covering:
1. Teams — proposed team names, short keys/identifiers, and a brief description of each team's scope.
2. Projects — for each team, proposed projects with a name, description, priority, owning team, and (if known) an owner and target dates, structured so cross-team dependencies between projects can be tracked later.
3. A short rationale note explaining how this structure supports tracking initiatives by status/priority/owner, coordinating cross-team dependencies, and letting engineers later create and assign tasks with due dates.

Present this as a clear, reviewable checklist/table (teams, then projects nested under each), using our configured credentials to look up any existing {{vendor}} workspace data (existing teams/projects) via the dashboard or API so you don't propose duplicates.

Done looks like: a complete, de-duplicated draft of teams and projects, with names, descriptions, priorities, and owners filled in wherever possible, ready for me to review.

Do not create, submit, or apply any teams or projects in {{vendor}} — only prepare the draft. Report back with the full draft plan and explicitly stop for human sign-off, noting any missing information you need from me before final approval.

ops_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure issue labels in {{vendor}}, our project tracker, as part of setting up the tracker's workflow structure. {{vendor}} is already set up with our workspace, teams, and projects; this step focuses only on labels.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization name if not already known, (2) the list of label categories I want (e.g., priority, type of work like bug/feature/chore, area or component, status flags like blocked/needs-review), and (3) whether labels should be workspace-wide or scoped to specific teams/projects.

Once I provide this, use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s label management (via the dashboard or API, whichever is available) and:
- Create each label with a clear, consistent name matching my naming convention.
- Assign a distinct color to each label to make them visually scannable in issue views.
- Group related labels logically (e.g., under a parent category) if {{vendor}} supports label grouping.
- Apply labels at the correct scope (workspace-wide vs. team/project-specific) as I specified.
- Avoid duplicating any labels that already exist in the workspace.

Done looks like: all requested labels exist in {{vendor}}, correctly named, colored, and scoped, ready to be applied to issues as part of the team's workflow customization.

Report back with: a list of labels created (name, color, scope), any labels skipped because they already existed, and any labels you could not create along with the reason (e.g., permission limits or naming conflicts). If you encounter any ambiguity about naming or scope that I didn't clarify, pause and ask me before proceeding further.

ops_002:n5.prompt:
You are helping me invite team members into {{vendor}}, our project tracker, with correct roles and access controls. A human must explicitly approve the invite list and permission settings before anything is sent, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the list of teammates to invite (name and email for each), (2) the intended role or permission level for each person (e.g., admin, member, viewer, or any custom role {{vendor}} supports), (3) whether SSO/SAML is enabled or should be configured for organization access, and (4) my domain or workspace name in {{vendor}}.

Using your configured credentials, sign in to {{vendor}} and: review the current workspace members and roles; draft the full invite list mapping each person to their proposed role and team/project scope; check whether SSO/SAML is already enabled for the organization and note its status; and prepare a checklist showing exactly what will change (new invites, role assignments, and any SSO/SAML configuration needed) if approved.

Do not send invitations, change permissions, or enable/modify SSO/SAML settings yourself. Present the draft invite list, proposed roles, and SSO/SAML status/checklist to me for review, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the full proposed invite list and roles, the current vs. proposed SSO/SAML status, any conflicts or missing information you found, and a clear statement that no invites or permission changes have been applied pending my approval.
